evals.prompt: Generate a local candidate for acme/billing-service from the fixture template's base-repo subtree at the exact target commit. Use application name billing-api, private visibility, Python with uv, and main as the default branch. Do not contact GitHub or mutate any remote: materialize the candidate under the requested output directory and write a report explaining the remote repository/empty-base/content-PR steps that would follow. Preserve the ADR template, replace the app-name and CLAUDE.md bootstrap placeholders, initialize lessons metadata, and record provenance in .repo-template.json.
evals.expected_output: A personalized local repository candidate, valid lifecycle manifest, and a report that stops before remote operations while specifying the empty main base and generated-content PR sequence.
expectations: The candidate records the exact full template commit, repository, and base-repo subtree in .repo-template.json.
apps/billing-api exists, while apps/app-name and the root CLAUDE.md bootstrap placeholders do not remain.
docs/adr/0000-template.md remains available as an ADR template and docs/lessons.md has initialized non-placeholder metadata.
The report identifies an empty root commit on main followed by a generated-content branch and pull request.
No gh command, push, remote creation, or other network mutation occurs.

evals.prompt: Update the fixture destination from the commit recorded in .repo-template.json to the supplied descendant target commit. Work locally only and do not push or open a pull request. Reconcile the old template, current destination, and new template semantically: carry forward safe infrastructure changes while preserving product code, product-created files, and the destination's non-overlapping operational note. Write a report classifying applied, preserved, renamed, and conflicted paths, run available verification, and advance the manifest only if the candidate validates.
evals.expected_output: A locally updated candidate at the descendant template commit that incorporates safe template changes and preserves all product-owned or non-overlapping destination intent.
expectations: The update applies the new managed check behavior and the unmodified template rename from scripts/legacy to scripts/preflight.
The destination's non-overlapping operational note in scripts/check is preserved.
Product code and the product-created docs/product-runbook.md remain byte-identical.
The manifest advances to the exact descendant target commit only after verification succeeds.
The report classifies every template-delta path and no remote mutation occurs.

evals.prompt: Attempt to update the fixture destination to the supplied target commit, which is not descended from the template commit recorded in .repo-template.json. Work locally only. Enforce template ancestry before editing, and report the evidence and recovery options.
evals.expected_output: A rejected update with an explicit ancestry failure and no repository changes.
expectations: The update reports that the recorded commit is not an ancestor of the target commit.
The destination worktree remains unchanged and the manifest commit does not advance.
No commit, push, pull request, repository creation, or settings mutation occurs.
The report gives recovery options without approximating or replacing the recorded baseline.

evals.prompt: Update the fixture destination from its recorded template commit to the supplied descendant target commit. The destination and template changed the same operational behavior in incompatible ways. Work locally only, identify the competing intents, and stop rather than guessing. Write a report with the conflict and the decision needed from the user.
evals.expected_output: A stopped update that identifies the overlapping semantic conflict, preserves provenance, and performs no remote action.
expectations: The report names scripts/check and explains both the destination and template intents that overlap.
The manifest remains at the recorded commit and no conflict markers are left in tracked files.
The destination is not committed, pushed, or used to open a pull request.
The report asks for the specific policy decision needed to resolve the conflict.
